style: Late-1990s East Coast boom bap, 86 BPM, rap. Vocal up front and dry: a deep, calm male baritone with light gravel, laying each line a hair behind the snare, unhurried, every word clear, finishing each rule and letting the beat breathe before the next. Parts: dusty sampled drum break, round kick, hard cracking snare on 2 and 4, loose swung hats. Upright bass loops a short two-bar phrase. Muted jazz piano chop, two chords, repeating. Faint vinyl crackle under everything. Arrangement: the loop never changes, short drum-only gaps between rules, beat rides out alone after the last line. Warm, slightly lo-fi, 12-bit grit, mono-leaning mix.
exclude: trap hi-hats, auto-tune, sung hook, singing, double-time flow, fast rap, 808 bass, synth pads, female vocals
lyrics:
[Intro: drum break alone for two bars, then calm baritone]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 1: laid back, behind the beat]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 2]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 3]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 4]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 5]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 6]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 7: slower, deliberate]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 8]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 9: slower, deliberate]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Two-bar drum break, then]
[Rule 10]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro: beat drops to bass and piano, spoken low]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[Drum break rides out, end]
title: tec-all10-B-baritone-behind-the-beat
